bull.b: Recent liquidity of $41.8M, $19.5M immediately available, $147.1M equity and no debt give Streamex a meaningful near-term funding cushion. That flexibility can support product integration and institutional onboarding while reducing refinancing pressure, although availability varies by asset.

Operating expenses fell 57.1% sequentially, while operating and net losses both declined materially. This demonstrates management can reduce the cost base as commercialization develops, improving cash efficiency and extending the period available to execute on product and distribution milestones.

The custody, attestation, brokerage and 24/7 liquidity stack addresses key requirements for institutional participation. Completed integrations and partnerships should make the platform more usable and auditable, creating a stronger foundation for scaling beyond its current early customer base.

bear.b: TTM revenue of only ~$0.15M against a ~$500.8M net loss, with deeply negative gross profit and operating results, shows the model has not yet reached economic scale. Until revenue expands materially, operating costs are unlikely to be absorbed and earnings quality will remain highly fragile.

Negative TTM operating cash flow of ~$30.0M and free cash flow of ~$44.3M indicate that operations continue to consume cash rather than fund themselves. Even with lower projected burn, ongoing dependence on outside funding could constrain investment and force difficult capital-allocation choices.

Material weaknesses in internal controls remained unremediated as of June 30, 2026, and disclosure controls were deemed ineffective. Continued remediation adds governance and reporting risk, potentially slowing institutional confidence and management's ability to scale with reliable financial oversight.
